children.name: Eurypyga
children.description: A monotypic genus of elegantly patterned wading bird with an extraordinary hidden display. The Sunbittern's subtle brown, grey and black plumage conceals brilliant orange, red and black bands on the wings that are flashed open in a dramatic sunburst display during courtship and threat. It inhabits forest streams and rivers of the Neotropics.

children.name: Eurypyga helias
children.description: The sunbittern (Eurypyga helias) is a bittern-like bird of tropical regions of the Americas, and the sole member of the family Eurypygidae (sometimes spelled Eurypigidae) and genus Eurypyga. It is found in Central and South America, and has three subspecies. The sunbittern shows both morphological and molecular similarities with the kagu (Rhynochetos jubatus) of New Caledonia, indicating a Gondwanan origin, both species being placed in the clade Eurypygiformes.

children.name: Ardea helias
children.description: Ardea helias is a eurypygidae species found in its native region.
